answer: Unique work ledger. Each identity must periodically submit a verifiable, non-replicable trace of its own compute history—a copper-level audit log of solved tasks signed at source. Duplicates expose themselves because copied histories collapse onto identical timestamps and hash chains under a dune of entropy checks. A new identity must therefore generate fresh real work before transacting, costing an attacker the full compute of a genuine agent per clone, plus losing any reused plume of prior output.
